description: Synchronous Science is on a mission to equip defence and national-security leaders with clear, actionable insights into electromagnetic sensing and communication challenges. Through a systems-thinking approach and extensive engineering expertise, we swiftly identify hidden vulnerabilities and untapped opportunities
entityDescription:
We perform research and development on a broad range of defence-related electromagnetic problems. These have included studies of the threats and vulnerabilities of contemporary and novel communication systems, including 4G LTE and 5G NR cellular, and the increasingly popular Internet of Things technologies such as LoRA and SigFox. A particular focus has been their potential use in adversaries' triggering mechanisms of RCIEDs and how to thwart this. In addition, we are interested in the resurgence of modern HF systems, the prediction of propagation-related phenomena, and the transmission of RF and microwave over optical links. Additional work has included the agile design and implementation of novel RF test and measurement environments over short timescales. 

Outside of work on communication systems, we have performed research into improved intelligence, surveillance, target acquisition, and reconnaissance techniques in synthetic aperture radar and optical domains. This has included research into the theoretical design and practical characterisation of novel low-observable materials. 

Our director has a PhD in Optoelectronics, an MSc (with distinction) in Communication Systems Engineering and a BSc in Mathematics. He has a solid theoretical, computational and experimental physics and engineering background and has contributed to academic and industrial works. He has also obtained memberships of the Institution of Engineering and Technology (IET), Institute of Physics (IoP) and Institute of Mathematics and Its Applications (IMA), as well as being a corporate member of ADS Group and Team Defense Information. 

We enjoy meeting with customers and suppliers to develop new generation-after-next solutions. Technological advancements are only made through discussions with the end-user.

entityDescription:
Epona AI Labs is an Irish deep-tech company based in Kinsale, Co. Cork, focused on developing next-generation contextual acoustic sensing systems for industrial applications. The company’s core innovation lies in fusing AI-driven acoustic analysis with environmental intelligence derived from ESA Sentinel satellite data. This approach enables more accurate machine health monitoring and hazard detection in complex environments such as quarries, construction sites, and agricultural settings.
Founded in 2023 by a multidisciplinary team with expertise in AI, acoustics, and industrial technology strategy, Epona is committed to building scalable, energy-efficient sensing solutions that operate effectively in visually degraded and remote locations. The company is currently advancing its prototype toward commercial deployment and has secured strategic collaborations with industry leaders and research institutions.
Epona has been awarded a grant from ESA BIC Ireland to support the integration of satellite data into its sensing platform, accelerating its development and market readiness. Through a combination of R&D, strategic IP development, and pilot deployments, Epona aims to position itself as a European leader in satellite-enhanced industrial sensing solutions.

description:
We develop the long-lasting heart of fuel cells and electrolysers. 
Hydrogen fuel cells and electrolysers play a key role in the global energy transition. The heart of both technologies is the membrane electrode assembly (MEA), which enables the conversion of hydrogen into electricity—and vice versa. The MEA is the component that largely determines the lifetime and cost of electrolysers and fuel cells. Duramea plans to revolutionise MEA production with a patent-pending technology: a polyaniline coating that protects the MEA against corrosion without impairing its performance. This innovation doubles MEA lifetime while maintaining efficiency. 
Our initial focus is to supply durable, high-performance MEAs for the scientific market. In the long term, Duramea aims to scale production and enable cost-efficient mass manufacturing of robust MEAs for applications on Earth, in lunar stations, and beyond. 
USP: Our patent-pending membrane electrode assembly doubles the service life of fuel cells and electrolysers.
entityDescription: Duramea, the newly established start-up, offers cutting-edge membrane electrode assemblies (MEAs) for polymer electrolyte fuel cells (PEMFC) and alkaline anion exchange membrane electrolysers (AEMWE). These MEAs play a crucial role in improving the efficiency and durability of systems that convert hydrogen into electrical energy and vice versa. Duramea's MEAs are suitable for a wide range of stationary and mobile applications, including ships, trucks, trains, and aircraft. Leveraging their innovative polyaniline (PANI)-based coating technology in MEA production, Duramea guarantees excellent corrosion resistance, extended lifespan, and outstanding performance.

entityDescription:
Everimpact, established in 2014, has a core mission to empower local authorities and industrial sectors to adopt more decisive climate action. This mission aligns with the goals of influential global organizations such as C40, R20, and ICLEI, which are all dedicated to driving climate action on a global scale.
However, the climate action efforts of French local authorities face significant hurdles due to the centralized nature of greenhouse gas reduction responsibility and a lack of resources. This centralized structure can stifle local initiatives and innovation, while resource constraints can limit the scope and ambition of climate action plans.
To address these challenges, Everimpact initially developed a solution that utilizes IoT sensors in urban spaces to gather data and inform climate action strategies. Proof of concept (POC) projects using this technology are currently underway in various cities around the world, demonstrating the potential of this approach.
Looking ahead, Everimpact recognizes that satellite measurement will be crucial for future success. Satellite technology can gradually reduce the reliance on IoT sensors while providing a broader and more comprehensive picture of greenhouse gas emissions and climate impacts. In particular, NewSpace, a burgeoning sector of the space industry, is poised to play a key role. NewSpace companies are developing innovative and cost-effective satellite technologies that can significantly improve the quality and frequency of measurements, all while driving down costs. This advancement will enable more accurate and timely data collection, which is essential for effective climate action planning and decision-making.

entityDescription:
Acusttel (Acústica y Telecomunicaciones, S.L.) is a Spanish engineering company founded in 1997 and headquartered in Gandía, Valencia. With more than 25 years of experience, it specializes in acoustic and vibration engineering, offering consulting, measurement, and turnkey solutions for environmental noise, building acoustics, and industrial sound control. Its accredited laboratory and test chambers, certified by ENAC, allow the company to perform product testing and acoustic certification in compliance with national and European regulations.

The company provides a broad range of services: acoustic design and insulation for buildings and industrial facilities, noise and vibration diagnostics, and environmental acoustic quality control. It develops customized solutions for ventilation systems, machinery, and other noise sources, supporting clients through every stage of a project—from initial measurements and modelling to final mitigation strategies. Acusttel also conducts design and analysis of materials’ acoustic behavior, evaluating how different construction or industrial materials absorb, transmit, or attenuate sound to optimize their performance in real-world applications.

A key differentiator is Acusttel’s underwater acoustics division. This specialized area covers the measurement and analysis of sound propagation in aquatic environments such as ports, offshore platforms, and marine construction sites. Using hydrophones and advanced modelling, the team assesses underwater noise, predicts sound transmission, and designs mitigation measures to protect marine ecosystems and comply with environmental regulations. These services are essential for activities like dredging, underwater piling, and coastal engineering projects.

Combining terrestrial and subaquatic expertise with advanced material analysis, Acusttel offers a complete acoustic engineering portfolio backed by rigorous technical standards and decades of know-how. Its mission is to improve environmental quality and reduce acoustic pollution on land and underwater, ensuring regulatory compliance while safeguarding human comfort and marine life.
